title: Environment communication configuration (environment/communication.yaml)
description: The environment-owned half of the communication plane, authored beside environment/topology.yaml. Profiles declare logical intent (outputs, routes, spaces as alias#destination); this file binds it physically: which provider plugin backs each ChatOps connection alias, where its credentials live, and which durable transport carries queued routes. Absent file = communication feature off for the environment; a profile declaring queued routes or ChatOps outputs then fails compilation loudly instead of guessing. Secrets never appear here - only references. In an agent-team repository this file lives at `harness-hg/communication.yaml`; the legacy path stays readable for repositories not yet migrated.

provider.description: The provider plugin behind this alias. `recording` captures messages locally instead of sending - rebinding a real alias to recording lets the same authored routes and eval fixtures run locally and in production.

name.description: Kubernetes Secret name holding the provider credential (in-cluster delivery).

key.description: Key within the named Secret whose value is the provider credential (in-cluster delivery).

env.description: Environment variable holding the credential on the operator host (CLI-side delivery, e.g. `hg chatops test`). Exactly one of name/key or env.

credentialRef.description: Where the provider credential lives - a Secret reference or an operator-host env var name. The VALUE never enters Git, plans, receipts, or logs. Required by every provider except recording.

inbound.description: Who may make this connection DO something (#348). Absent means no inbound authorization is declared, and the gateway refuses every inbound request on this connection - a connection with no policy is deny-all, never allow-all. Outbound delivery is unaffected: a connection can post without accepting instructions, which is the common case.

approvedUsers.description: Provider-native user IDENTIFIERS (a Discord snowflake), never display names. A display name is changeable by the person it names, so authorizing one authorizes whoever holds it next.

approvedRoles.description: Provider-native role identifiers. A role is the maintainable form of the same grant: membership changes without a redeploy.

approvedChannels.description: Where a request is accepted FROM. An approved user in an unapproved channel is refused: the channel is what makes a request auditable by the people who can see it.

mentionPolicy.description: Whether the agent must be addressed explicitly. `any-message` makes every message in an approved channel an instruction, which is occasionally what you want and is never a safe default.

threadPolicy.description: `inherit` accepts a thread if its parent channel is approved. `refuse` requires the thread itself to be listed - threads are created by anyone with access, so inheriting is convenient and slightly wider than it looks.

chatopsConnections.description: Connection aliases routes reference as <alias>#<destination>. The alias is the whole ChatOps configuration surface - no provider-specific fields leak into profile contracts.

plugin.description: The durable transport plugin backing queued delivery (e.g. redis-streams). The compiler holds each plugin's capability table (queued/fifo/dlq/replay) and refuses a route requiring a capability the plugin lacks - a guarantee is never silently weakened.

config.description: Plugin-specific, secret-free configuration (host, stream prefix, retention). Credentials, if any, ride a credentialRef-shaped entry inside - never a literal.

durableProvider.description: The environment's durable transport. Profiles say only `delivery: {mode: queued}`; this says what physically carries it.
